day.reading: Wright's analogy needs a fitness signal at every step; Eden said Wright misunderstood the path-length argument; cumulative selection is not random typing either way
day.number: the path-length reading has no number: Eden offers none ('many powers of 10' above 120, M-406, claim file D3b q4), so no count is computed for it here

critic.reading: with a per-step signal a specified protein is reached in about 1250 steps, not 10^325 (Wright); Ulam: random construction is not the problem

notes: Both sides' numbers reproduce. 250 x 5 = 1250 questions is above the information bound log2 20^250 = 1080.5 bits and above the 1162.7 bits of Eden's 10^350, so it holds for either of Eden's figures; random assembly needs 10^325.3 trials. Eden accepted the arithmetic (p.8) and moved the question to path length and per-step viability (M-405, M-404), which neither Wright's count nor Eden supplies a number for. Wright's 3e9 x 1e-5 = 3e4 mutants per locus per generation bears on mutation supply, not on the signal.
